To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
embedded resistors have been realized on high loss epoxy and low loss BCB board level dielectric using electroless plating and foil transfer techniques.

the embedded resistors can be realized in a low-cost process using Ni-P alloys and NiCr and AlSi foils, and the electroless plating process can be adopted by the PCB manufacturing industries without any additional investment.
embedded thin film resistances have been successfully demonstrated on both conventional high loss epoxy and low loss BCB board level dielectric.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of low cost, high performance, embedded resistors on high and low loss dielectrics for advanced SOP applications.
the development of a low-cost, high performance embedded thin film resistor process on both high-loss and low-loss dielectrics.

the development of low-cost, low profile, high reliability and low loss thin film resistor materials and processes for the integration of embedded resistors into high density SOP module using sequential build-up technology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the embedded thin film resistive structures can be successfully realized on both conventional high loss and proposed low loss dielectric substrates.
embedded thin film resistive structures have been realized in high loss epoxy and low loss BCB board level dielectrics with low-cost, large format electroless NiP and NiPWP alloys.
the electroless plating of NiP and electroplating of Cu can be used for the embedding of thin film resistors in the BCB dielectric for SOP modules.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that embedded thin film resistive elements can be fabricated on both conventional board level dielectric and BCB.
we have developed a novel low-cost process for embedded resistors on high-loss epoxy and proposed low-loss BCB dielectrics.
we have demonstrated the use of electroless Ni-P and Ni-W-P alloys as thin film resistors in a variety of applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the embedded resistors can be integrated into PCBs using sequential build-up (SBU) process with low-cost materials and process.

we have demonstrated the use of a low-cost large-format electroless plating process for deposition of nickel-phosphorus (NiP) and tungsten phosphide (NiWP) thin films as a seed layer on BCB dielectric and as embedded resistors on high and low loss dielectrics.
the electroless plating process can be adopted for embedded resistor fabrication on BCB dielectrics.
